summary: Two-project integration brief: Agent Loop proposes autonomous work (README.md:51-56), while Tool Gate deterministically evaluates caller-supplied tool metadata and invocation envelopes and emits allow, deny, or review_required receipts without executing tools (README.md:5-13,17-20). Their shared safety boundary is the transition from an agent’s proposed action to runtime permission before side effects occur (README.md:17-20,31-33). Recommendation: require every Agent Loop tool intent to pass through Tool Gate using catalog-owned metadata, and make the runtime accept execution only with a matching allow receipt; route review_required receipts to an operator. Agent Loop risk: any execution path that bypasses receipt enforcement can run proposed work without policy review (README.md:31-33). Tool Gate risk: it trusts caller-provided risk, mutation, idempotency, review, and target metadata (src/types.rs:21-40; src/policy.rs:49-167) while providing no authentication, authorization, sandboxing, or execution isolation (README.md:156-158), so forged or incorrect metadata can produce an unsafe allow decision. Declared clean-tree check passed with git diff --exit-code HEAD --. Inspection was read-only and created no artifacts.
